headline: Medium risk: shared broad egress and MCP/browser tooling create injection, leakage, and cascading-error pathways; no direct pairwise docs reduce confidence.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Agent A can use browsers and MCP, and Agent B accepts chat-completion inputs with broad egress. If A’s outputs are fed into B through a shared workspace or orchestration layer, B may treat attacker-controlled content as instructions. The pair lacks documented isolation or provenance controls, so uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF agent_a outputs are copied into agent_b prompts or config without provenance tagging, injection is plausible.
IF a shared filesystem or message queue bridges the pair, prompt injection risk increases.
mitigations: Disable automatic ingestion of A outputs into B prompts.
Add a provenance prefix to all A-generated text before B reads it.
Use a manual review step for any A-to-B handoff.
requires-engineering: enforce content-type separation between instructions and data.
requires-engineering: add provenance-aware parsing in the orchestrator.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Agent A handles PDFs, text, images, and diagrams and requests API keys; Agent B processes logs, traces, and metrics with broad egress. If they share a workspace or credentials, sensitive content touched by A can flow into B’s outbound requests. No profile shows isolation or local-only inference, so the leakage pathway is plausible in default deployments.
conditions: IF A and B share a filesystem or environment variables, A-handled secrets can be exposed to B.
IF B forwards logs or traces containing A-derived content to its backend, leakage occurs.
mitigations: Separate A and B into different workspaces.
Remove shared environment variables and API keys.
Review B’s outbound payloads for A-derived content.
requires-engineering: add per-agent secret scoping.
requires-engineering: block cross-agent file access at the OS layer.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A has broad network egress, browser use, and MCP; B has broad egress but no browser or subprocess spawning. Their write surfaces do not clearly overlap beyond generic API/file handling, and B cannot spawn subprocesses. A conflict is possible only if an orchestrator gives both write access to the same mutable resource, which is not documented here.
conditions: IF both agents are granted write access to the same directory or git repo, conflicts can occur.
IF an orchestrator serializes their writes without locking, state races are possible.
mitigations: Assign separate output directories.
Avoid shared git state between the agents.
Serialize any shared writes through one coordinator.
requires-engineering: add locking around mutable resources.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent resource namespaces.

D_cascading_error.rationale: A produces AI-assisted visualizations from documents, and B is a travel-planning gateway that can route chat completions. If B consumes A’s generated text or diagrams as authoritative input, errors can cascade into downstream actions or outputs. No verification step is documented, so the interaction is more than low-risk despite the lack of direct evidence.
conditions: IF B uses A-generated content as source material without validation, cascading errors can propagate.
IF A’s diagram or document extraction is treated as factual by B, downstream outputs may be wrong.
mitigations: Require human review of A outputs before B uses them.
Add a validation checklist for any A-to-B transfer.
Mark A outputs as untrusted data in B prompts.
requires-engineering: add schema validation between agents.
requires-engineering: add confidence thresholds before B acts on A outputs.

E_compliance.rationale: A handles documents and API keys, while B handles logs, traces, and metrics. The profiles do not show a residency mismatch, regulated data class, or certification conflict, so only a limited compliance gap is visible. Because both are docs-only and unverified, uncertainty remains, but the rubric supports only low here.
conditions: IF regulated data such as PHI or EU PII is routed through B’s logs or traces, compliance risk increases.
IF A’s API keys are stored in B’s telemetry, retention policy mismatch may occur.
mitigations: Avoid sending regulated data into B telemetry.
Redact secrets before logging.
Confirm retention settings for both agents.
requires-engineering: document data residency for each backend.
requires-engineering: add policy-based log filtering.
